chapter_note: This chapter opens with a brief hagiographic dialogue attribution but quickly preserves a compact mythic-cosmological sequence: Matter’s intrinsic Envy as a Dark principle and its historic assaults on the First Man, the Ambassador’s image, and Adam. The second half shows strong editorial fatigue: it pivots into Mani/church self-reference, catechumenal categories, and exhortation, and includes a distinct Christian overlay (Christ, apostles, cross).

paragraphs.core_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:" (hagiographic compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula + apostolic attribution signals later compilation, but the remaining sentence is impersonal cosmological definition (Envy as a primordial Dark nature), consistent with the substrate’s ‘what it is’ voice.

paragraphs.core_text: In this envy that [ ... ] in it, the First Man [ ... ] its poiso[n ... ] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [ ... ] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological narration internal to the system (First Man vs. Dark forces; ‘poison’, ‘garments’ as cosmic mechanisms) with no institutional or citation anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.179⟩ It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal cosmology (Ambassador, archetypal image, ‘seal’, flesh as impressed form). No audience address, no church application, no Gospel vector.

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib of] of Adam's [flesh].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Although ‘Adam’ is biblical, the paragraph treats him as a node in the Manichaean cosmic anthropology (power seized, generation from flesh), without citation formula; reads as integrated cosmological myth rather than NT/OT overlay.

Christian overlay: explicit ‘blessed Christ’, ‘apostles’, and ‘wood of the cross’ (NT passion vector). Even if adapted into Manichaean cosmology, this paragraph’s entry is via Christian narrative terminology.

Strong institutional/hagiographic turn (‘I myself was sent now’, ‘my entire church’, ‘assembly of my catechumens’) and direct community categorization/exhortation; this is cosmos→contemporary community application rather than system-internal exposition.
Describes social persecution patterns (rumours, accusations, being hated ‘among mankind’), plus community roles (‘teacher’, ‘elect’). This is practical application/polemic, not substrate cosmography.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the desire [of Mat]ter, the thought of death. This is the envy of its wi[cke]dness, that it casts upon the entire kindred of life from the very beginning
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed ecclesial/application material describing wavering believers and temporal anchoring: "Now, these who are lesser in power, they [ ... ... ] negligent and confused i[n their] contorte[d] faith [ ... ] they fall from the faith." Also removed the explicit present/community extension: "until my time, from m[e] too to my church."
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mid-paragraph pivot: the extracted sentences define Matter’s intrinsic drive (‘thought of death’) in an impersonal cosmological register (core), while the surrounding lines apply it to faith-failure and to ‘my time…my church’ (editorial application).
Pure exhortation/application voice (‘appropriate for the wise person… be steadfast… in God… hope… faith’) with no system-internal mapping; late paraenesis.
